answer.text:
Acme did sign off UAT, but only for core replenishment, not for the programme as a whole. The signed document confirmed that user acceptance testing for core replenishment was completed satisfactorily for the 25 store pilot cohort, covering ambient and dry goods categories. It explicitly stated that the sign-off does not extend to fresh categories, which remain in scope for a later phase, and does not constitute acceptance of the overall programme. Lena Fischer, Acme's Head of Supply Chain, signed it on 22 January 2025. [1] [2]

The exact wording Ana Duarte sent for signature on 21 January 2025 was: "Acme Org confirms that user acceptance testing for core replenishment has been completed satisfactorily for the 25 store pilot cohort, covering ambient and dry goods categories. This sign-off does not extend to fresh categories, which remain in scope for a later phase, and does not constitute acceptance of the overall programme." Lena Fischer replied the next day: "Signed and attached. The wording is what I asked for, thank you for being careful with it." [1] [2]

The scope was deliberately narrowed at Lena Fischer's request. In the UAT readiness review on 21 January 2025 she asked what exactly she was signing, saying: "I am signing that ambiant core replenishment works for twenty-five stores, not that the project is finished." Ana Duarte confirmed: "That is exactly what you are signing." In the same meeting Lena Fischer had confirmed she would be the signatory, saying "I do" when asked who signs UAT off, and that she would sign something sent to her in writing. [3] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8]

Two caveats on completeness. First, at the time of signing, two UAT defects remained open, both the same root cause on case pack and minimum order quantity rounding; Ana Duarte's email sending the wording for signature noted both were scheduled for fix that week and neither was a blocker. Kwame Boateng reported on 24 January 2025: "Both rounding defects fixed and re-tested. Nine of nine scenarios now pass." So the sign-off was given with two known non-blocking defects, fixed and re-tested three days later. [1] [9]

Second, no separate UAT sign-off for the fresh phase appears anywhere in the supplied archive. Fresh UAT ran in autumn 2025, and the go/no-go meeting on 17 November 2025 approved produce, dairy and chilled ready meals for the 15 December go-live, with bakery descoped. That was a go/no-go decision recorded in the meeting, not a signed UAT acceptance document. If a fresh UAT sign-off exists, it is not in the supplied evidence. [10] [11] [12] [13]
